- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp upward sentiment spikes; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment momentum to forecast.
- After a model forecast spike (≥ 2% above recent mean), true price often corrects downward; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; use 28-day rolling mean to smooth out noise.
- When sentiment shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model fails to mean-revert; apply mean-reversion bias toward 30-day historical average.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in first 7 days of horizon; apply 1–2% downward bias for early days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
